sources_considered.why: Primary analysis identifies concrete security and quality problems in generated code.
Peer-reviewed controlled study supplies material counterevidence on downstream maintainability.
Read successfully. Its single-task Gemini comparison is narrower than the causal claim and adds no industry-wide identification.
Search result describes later reporting; primary studies were preferred, and the result was not used as evidence.

evidence_items.publisher: Sabra, Schmitt and Tyler via arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, Assessing the Quality and Security of AI-Generated Code
evidence_items.explanation: Static analysis of generated Java assignments found defects and security vulnerabilities, supporting concern about unchecked generated code. It does not establish unavoidable danger or a causal decline in software overall.

The controlled study found no measurable downstream maintainability penalty for its AI-assisted development tasks. That limits blanket deterioration claims, but the study does not test autonomous vibe coding or the entire software industry.

unresolved_gaps: No representative baseline demonstrating the asserted overall deterioration was established.
No retrieved study isolates AI-generated code as a material cause of an industry-wide decline.
Evidence about AI-assisted development does not necessarily describe unreviewed, substantially AI-authored programs.
The disrespect judgment has no empirical resolution.
